intent: Bring focus_owner/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/kuhy/focus_owner/FocusPolicy.kt (277 lines) under the repo-wide 250-line cap with no change to how a policy is parsed or applied.
scope: focus_owner/.../FocusPolicy.kt — reduced to the FocusPolicy data class, its predicates and its companion-object loader
focus_owner/.../PolicyTypes.kt — new: SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION, PolicyFormatException, CurfewWindow, HomeLocation
Non-goal: any change to parsing, to the curfew wrap-around rule, or to the allowlist predicates
Non-goal: DevicePolicyBridge.kt and EnforcementRunner.kt, which measurement rules out (see risks)
changes: Moved the four top-level declarations the policy is built from — the schema-version constant, the exception it raises, the CurfewWindow with its midnight-wrapping contains(), and the HomeLocation with its hasCoordinates guard — into PolicyTypes.kt.

No call site changed and no import was added: both files are package com.kuhy.focus_owner, and Kotlin resolves top-level declarations across files in the same package. This is the same seam that worked for EnforcementDecision.kt earlier in this series.

Deliberately did NOT extract the companion-object loader (load/loadFile/parse), even though it is the larger block. Callers write FocusPolicy.parse(...) at eight sites including four in the tests; moving it to a top-level function would have rewritten all of them, turning a zero-risk move into a real refactor.

verification.evidence: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, and per-class counts unchanged: EnforcementDecisionCurfewTest 13, EnforcementDecisionTest 12, EnforcementLogTest 9, EnforcementRunnerBestTest 6 — 40 tests, 0 failures. --rerun-tasks again required, since a plain gradlew test reports UP-TO-DATE.
All configured hooks pass. Zero suppressions.
FocusPolicy.kt 238, PolicyTypes.kt 48 — both under the 250-line cap, down from a single 277-line file.

verification.command: Call-site check for the loader before choosing the seam
verification.evidence: grep found FocusPolicy.parse at four test sites and FocusPolicy.load at three production sites. This corrected an earlier reading: a declaration-name scan had counted `parse` as untested, but it is exercised by every fixture in EnforcementFixtures.kt. The proxy undercounts transitive exercise, which is why the seam question rather than the file-level percentage decided this split.

risks: FocusPolicy.kt at 238 lines has only 12 lines of headroom. Adding two or three more policy fields would put it back over the cap, at which point the loader extraction — and its eight call-site rewrites — becomes the next move.

The remaining two over-cap Kotlin files are not split. DevicePolicyBridge.kt (415) references one tested declaration out of 28: it wraps Android's DevicePolicyManager, which JVM unit tests cannot instantiate, so any split there moves code no test executes. EnforcementRunner.kt (564) is exercised by six tests focused on one selection function; its location-acquisition and alarm paths need an instrumented device.
focus_owner has no CI workflow and no Kotlin linter (no jacoco, ktlint or detekt), so the gradle and Flutter suites are the entire verifier for this change.
rollback: git revert the commit — one edited file and one added file, with no data, config or schema migration.
After rollback, re-run gradlew test --rerun-tasks and flutter test; expect 40 and 94 tests passing.
